NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
MECHANISM CLASS: Configuration change of flue-gas quench setpoint and recirculation duty.
— Standard practice typically operates secondary chamber quench and recirculation systems within a broad "standard" band (e.g., quench outlet 400-500°C, recirculation at 20% of flow) to maintain boiler efficiency.
— The proposed mitigation is a genuine departure: it shifts the operating point to a "fast-cool" regime by lowering the quench setpoint to 250°C and increasing recirculation duty to 35%, specifically to minimize gas residence time within the 250–450°C de-novo synthesis window.
— Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest existing practice is "cold quench" in glass or metals processing; the difference here is that the mitigation exploits a *schedule/duty* interaction (recirculation enhancing quench rate) rather than adding new hardware or changing the quench medium's composition.
— The mechanism attacks the driving physics by reducing the time-temperature integral $ \int_{T_{max}}^{T_{min}} \tau(T) dT $ in the 250-450°C range, thereby lowering the probability of chlorophenol polymerization into dioxins.

PHYSICS CHECK
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = residence time in the 250–450°C temperature window ($\tau_{window}$); the mechanism moves it DOWN by lowering the quench setpoint to 250°C and increasing recirculation duty to 35% (which reduces the volume fraction of high-temperature gas, accelerating the cooling rate); this REDUCES the de-novo reformation rate.
Governing relation: The dioxin formation rate $R$ is proportional to $\int_{250}^{450} \exp(-E_a/RT) \, dt$. Lowering the quench setpoint from ~450°C to 250°C removes the entire 250–450°C window from the "hot hold" zone, replacing it with a "fast pass-through" zone. Increasing recirculation duty from 20% to 35% reduces the residence time $\tau$ in the secondary chamber by approximately 30% (via dilution and increased velocity), further reducing the integral. The sign of the change in $\tau_{window}$ is negative, which lowers the damage/failure integral.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
— (c) Set flue-gas quench water outlet temperature setpoint to 250°C (down from standard 400°C). This is a parameter change on the existing quench control system.
— (c) Increase secondary flue-gas recirculation (FGR) duty to 35% of total flue-gas flow (up from standard 20%). This is a configuration change on the existing recirculation blower and dampers.
— (c) Execute burnout-temperature procedure: maintain secondary chamber exit temperature at 250°C for a minimum of 2 seconds before entering the air pollution control device. This is a procedural change to the interlock logic, ensuring the "cold" condition is sustained.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
— The implementation bill contains zero new hardware, zero new materials, and zero new instrumentation.
— Operational loss pricing: Increasing recirculation duty from 20% to 35% increases blower power consumption. Order of magnitude: ~15% increase in recirculation blower energy. This is negligible compared to total incinerator boiler heat input (<0.1% of total energy). The quench setpoint reduction increases water consumption slightly, but this is offset by the reduced need for downstream scrubbing due to lower pollutant load. Net operational loss is near-zero; the trade nets positive because dioxin compliance avoids regulatory penalties and filter changeout costs.
— Parity conclusion: Same-or-lower burden class. No development burden. All changes are parameter/procedure adjustments on existing equipment.
EXECUTABLE TEST
— Protocol: 1. Establish baseline dioxin concentration at standard settings (Quench 400°C, FGR 20%). 2. Apply mitigation settings (Quench 250°C, FGR 35%). 3. Run continuous dioxin monitoring for 72 hours using existing CEMS or periodic filter bag sampling analysis (GC-MS). 4. Pass/Fail threshold: Dioxin TEQ concentration must drop by ≥50% compared to baseline, AND residence time in 250-450°C window must be verified by temperature profiles to be <1 second. 5. Duration: 72 hours of stable operation. 6. Kill criterion: If dioxin TEQ does not decrease or if boiler efficiency drops >2% (due to quench cooling), the mechanism is invalid.

INPUT-AVAILABILITY CHECK
— Required signals: Flue-gas temperature (existing), Recirculation flow rate (existing), Dioxin concentration (existing monitoring or periodic sampling). All are within the permitted set and stated infrastructure.

MECHANISM-DIVERSITY CLAUSE
— MECHANISM CLASS: Configuration change. This is the first/only row in this set, so diversity is satisfied.
